title: Zhang Juan v. Peng Yu, private lending · Loans and default

sources.name: Promissory note (first loan, 40,000 yuan)
sources.quote: On 3 November 2020 the borrower Peng Yu borrowed RMB 40,000 from the lender Zhang Juan (in words: forty thousand yuan; in figures: 40,000), for a term of one month, to be repaid by 3 December 2020.

sources.name: Promissory note (second loan, 40,000 yuan)
sources.quote: On 13 November 2020 the borrower Peng Yu borrowed RMB 40,000 from the lender Zhang Juan (in words: forty thousand yuan; in figures: 40,000), for a term of one month, to be repaid by 13 December 2020.

sources.name: China Construction Bank customer transaction statement
sources.quote: On 3 November 2020 the plaintiff transferred RMB 40,000 to the defendant by bank transfer.

sources.name: WeChat and Alipay transfer records
sources.quote: The plaintiff paid Chen Sixuan, a person not party to the case, RMB 34,000 by bank transfer and RMB 6,000 by WeChat transfer; Chen Sixuan then paid the defendant RMB 33,800 by Alipay transfer, RMB 2,000 by WeChat transfer and RMB 4,200 in cash.

sources.name: First-instance judgment in this case

loc.court: Hecheng District People's Court, Huaihua City, Hunan Province

sources.quote: After the two loans fell due the defendant repaid neither on time; this court supports the plaintiff's claim that the defendant repay the principal of the two loans, RMB 80,000.

events.label: Zhang Juan transfers 40,000 yuan; Peng Yu gives a note
events.detail: Zhang Juan delivered RMB 40,000 by bank transfer; Peng Yu issued a promissory note stating the amount, the term and the repayment date.

events.label: Peng Yu borrows another 40,000 yuan via a non-party
events.detail: Because Peng Yu's bank card was frozen, Zhang Juan, as instructed, transferred the money to Chen Sixuan (Zhang Juan's daughter), a person not party to the case; Chen Sixuan then passed it to Peng Yu by Alipay, WeChat and cash, and Peng Yu issued a second promissory note.

events.label: First 40,000 yuan falls due, unpaid
events.detail: When the loan fell due Peng Yu did not repay as agreed; neither loan's principal has been repaid.

events.label: Second 40,000 yuan falls due, unpaid
events.detail: The second loan was likewise not repaid at maturity; the court ordered Peng Yu to pay overdue interest on each principal from its own maturity date at the LPR.
